rows.practice: assesses client needs and risk, agrees a contract with review points and conducts an episode of therapy within a named ethical code, taking the work to supervision
rows.knowledge: the ethical and legal frame of therapy, from confidentiality limits and data law to safe boundaries, together with several models of mental distress and of the relationship
rows.identity: a counsellor in training who knows their own strengths, limits and biases, looks after their own well-being and holds professional responsibility to clients, employers and society

rows.practice: repairs ruptures in the alliance without defensiveness, works openly with differences of power and identity between counsellor and client and finds creative, principled routes through ethical dilemmas
rows.knowledge: critical views of assessment tools and outcome measures, the research base behind practice and how social, political and economic forces shape mental health services
rows.identity: a self-directing practitioner who confronts discrimination at professional and systemic levels and turns a commitment to equality into anti-discriminatory therapeutic work

rows.practice: designs and evaluates a sizeable empirical study or systematic review, uses audit to improve therapy and works in depth with chronic distress and intense emotion through reflexive use of self
rows.knowledge: the discourses of diagnosis and psychopathology, the history and philosophy behind both the field and their own approach, plus research at the edge of current knowledge in therapy
rows.identity: a reflexive therapist who speaks out about discriminatory harm and power in services, training and supervision and steers their own continuing academic and professional growth

subjectSpecific.text: Your personal development work should help you take charge of your own learning.
It should help you work with clients safely and ethically.
It should help you tell your own feelings apart from your client's and see yourself in relation to others.
It should help you see yourself as a resource in the work.
It should help you become aware of your own personal and social identity.
It should help you find and deal with hidden biases and prejudice in yourself and your work.
It should give you a true sense of how competent you are.
It should help you accept yourself, which helps you accept your clients.
It should help you build a self-care plan that guards against burnout and keeps you emotionally strong.
It should help you become organised, adaptable and resilient.
It should lead you to keep building self-awareness through reflection all your working life.
It should help you see yourself as a whole person within your profession and society.
It should help you live with uncertainty, ambiguity, risk and failure.
It should make you sensitive to your values, including ethical, social, diversity and environmental ones.
It should help you see your enterprising strengths and use them flexibly.
You must be able to show emotional competence and warmth, and to work through personal issues that therapy work raises in you.
You must be able to use your personal and professional resources creatively to meet many kinds of client.
You must be able to spot what triggers you in client work and deal with it through self-care, supervision or your own therapy.
You must be able to show that you know what being a client feels like, from group work, supervision or your own therapy.
You must be able to show that you know how your own life and identity can affect the therapy you offer.
You must be able to reflect on yourself and the relationship in all your client work, keep your needs apart from your client's, and use supervision and personal support when you need it.
You must be able to take responsibility and use feedback well.
You must be able to recognise your limits, your power and your strengths.
You must be able to build creativity, flexibility, motivation and independence, and work proactively.
You must be able to show your professional development.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: therapy settings read in their wider context
statements.paraphrase: The settings where therapy happens and the services they run, from brief to long-term work with individuals, couples, families, groups or communities, should be understood against their history, culture, economics and politics.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the places of practice as shaped by history and by social, economic and political forces, not as neutral venues.

forBeneficiary.text: You should learn to read any service you work in against its history, culture, economics and politics.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: choosing a mode of delivery with care
statements.paraphrase: Each way of delivering therapy, in a room or remotely, live or not, carries its own protocols, risks and benefits; these must be weighed with care to find the right mix for the client, the practitioner's competence and the relationship.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure trainees learn to weigh in-person and remote modes against client need, their own competence and the relationship before choosing how to work.

forBeneficiary.text: Before you choose to work in person or by video, phone or text, you must weigh the risks and benefits for that client and for your own competence.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: training that joins study, growth and a supervised placement
statements.paraphrase: Training will join academic study with personal and skills development so that students can complete an assessed, supervised client placement, and it should build the UNESCO key competencies so that graduates keep learning, reflectively and reflexively, across their careers.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course so that its academic, personal and skills strands all lead towards a supervised, assessed placement, and plan where the UNESCO sustainability competencies are built.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course will bring together study, personal growth and skills work to ready you for a supervised placement with clients, and should leave you able to keep learning about yourself and your practice.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: what all training offers and what the competent graduate can do
statements.paraphrase: Whatever its modality or mode, every course will give chances to engage with the literature, learn research methods, build client skills and grow personally and professionally; the competent graduate will be able to work effectively with clients in a safe, contracted relationship while caring for themselves.

forPractitioner.text: Check that the course gives every trainee the literature, research methods, client skills and personal growth, whatever the modality, and that graduates leave able to work safely under contract and look after themselves.

forBeneficiary.text: Whatever approach you train in, you will meet the research literature, learn how research is done, build skills with clients and grow as a person; by the end you will be able to work well with clients within a safe agreement while looking after yourself.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: experiential learning, inclusive content and authentic assessment
statements.paraphrase: Courses prize experiential learning beside academic results and make room for openness and vulnerability; content tries to keep minority experience in view and to question theory rooted in majority culture; assessment needs to be authentic, accessible and tied to the work of a therapist.

forPractitioner.text: Build in experiential learning that allows vulnerability, test the curriculum for majority-culture bias, and make each assessment authentic, accessible and close to real therapeutic work.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: a reflective view of the profession's sustainable future
statements.paraphrase: Courses seek to build knowledge of sustainable development in the profession, setting it in its history and culture and inviting critique of its structures and dominant discourses; this will call for a reflective and reflexive attitude that imagines how the profession and its graduates can keep bringing broad benefit to people and society.

forPractitioner.text: Invite students to critique the profession's institutions and dominant ideas about mental illness, research and treatment, and to imagine how therapy can grow in ways that benefit individuals, communities and society.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be asked to look critically at how your profession is organised and talked about, and to think about how it, and you, can keep doing good for people and communities over time.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.paraphrase: All eight UNESCO competencies for sustainability (among them systems, anticipatory, normative and strategic thinking, collaboration, critical thought, self-awareness and joined-up problem-solving) are held to be essential; the qualified therapist needs to use them all in practice, so the learning setting and curriculum need to show them too.

forPractitioner.text: Map the eight UNESCO competencies across modules and placement, and make sure the course's own facilities and ways of working model them.

forBeneficiary.text: You will need to use all eight sustainability competencies, such as systems thinking, collaboration and self-awareness, in your work as a therapist, and your course should let you see and practise them.

Sustainability: Developing learning environments to promote sustainable development

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: responsibility for one's own and others' well-being as a developmental aim
statements.paraphrase: Training needs facilities for adult-centred and experiential learning across digital, individual, group and community settings; courses aim to set theory and practice in their social, economic and political arena and to support employability, and fostering responsibility for one's own and others' psychological well-being must be a developmental aim.

forPractitioner.text: Provide spaces for experiential and adult learning across digital, personal, group and community settings, and make students' growing responsibility for their own and others' well-being an explicit aim of the course.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course must help you grow a sense of responsibility for other people's psychological well-being and for your own.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Counselling and Psychotherapy degree

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: knowing and showing the value of therapeutic skills
statements.paraphrase: Students should grasp both the commercial and the practical worth of their skills and be able to explain and show them to employers and in plans to work for themselves or set up a private practice; they should also be helped to see their own enterprising capacities and to use them flexibly as contexts change.

forPractitioner.text: Give students tasks that make them state the market and practical value of their therapeutic skills, for job applications and for private practice plans, and help them notice their own enterprising strengths.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to explain and show what your skills are worth, both to an employer and in a plan for your own practice, and to notice where you are enterprising.

statements.about: digital competency for communication and employability
statements.paraphrase: Building digital and transferable skills should include using technology to share ideas in creative, innovative and accessible ways that support study and employment.

forPractitioner.text: Set tasks in which students use digital tools to present ideas creatively and accessibly, and link them to study success and employability.

forBeneficiary.text: You should learn to use digital tools to put your ideas across creatively and accessibly, in ways that help your studies and your job prospects.

statements.paraphrase: Building these professional capacities should be central to curriculum design and may run through the whole course; outcomes, activities and authentic assessment for employability and enterprise may sit in dedicated modules and across others.

forPractitioner.text: Plan employability and enterprise into the curriculum from the start, through dedicated modules, threads across modules or both, with matching outcomes and authentic assessment.

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: the five pillars of the curriculum
statements.paraphrase: Courses will typically offer an integrated curriculum resting on five pillars: theory, skills practice, personal growth, professional growth and research.

forPractitioner.text: Structure the curriculum around the five pillars and show how they connect.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to show fitting emotional competence and warmth, including working through personal issues that the work stirs up.

forPractitioner.text: Assess emotional competence and warmth in practice, and support students to work through what the work stirs up.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to show emotional competence and warmth, and to work through personal issues that therapy work raises in you.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to use their personal and professional resources creatively and flexibly to meet a wide range of clients' needs.

forPractitioner.text: Look for flexible use of self and skills across different clients.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to use your personal and professional resources creatively to meet many kinds of client.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: personal triggers and how to manage them
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to spot their own triggers in client work and handle them through self-care, supervision or personal therapy.

forPractitioner.text: Teach students to name triggers and act on them through supervision or therapy.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to spot what triggers you in client work and deal with it through self-care, supervision or your own therapy.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: knowing what it is to be a client
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to show awareness of what being a client is like, gained through supervision, group and experiential work and possibly personal therapy.

forPractitioner.text: Give students ways to experience the client's position, such as experiential groups or personal therapy.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to show that you know what being a client feels like, from group work, supervision or your own therapy.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: how one's own history affects therapy
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to show awareness of how their past and present experience can affect therapy and be shaped by age, family, culture, disadvantage, gender, race, sexuality and social position.

forPractitioner.text: Explore students' life experience and identity and how these enter the work.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to show that you know how your own life and identity can affect the therapy you offer.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to make reflection on themselves and the relationship central to clinical work, tell their needs from the client's, own their learning and use supervision, development and personal support or therapy as needed.

forPractitioner.text: Assess reflective practice and the use of supervision and personal support throughout placement.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to reflect on yourself and the relationship in all your client work, keep your needs apart from your client's, and use supervision and personal support when you need it.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: personal responsibility and use of feedback
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to take personal responsibility and engage constructively with feedback.

forPractitioner.text: Assess how students respond to and act on feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to take responsibility and use feedback well.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: knowing one's limits, power and strengths
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to recognise their own limits, power and strengths.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to name their limits, power and strengths with evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to recognise your limits, your power and your strengths.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to build practical creativity, flexibility, motivation, autonomy and a proactive way of working.

forPractitioner.text: Give room for autonomous, creative work in placement and projects.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to build creativity, flexibility, motivation and independence, and work proactively.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Trainees must be able to show professional development.

forPractitioner.text: Track professional development across the course.

forBeneficiary.text: You must be able to show your professional development.

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: an integrated curriculum with an assessed, supervised placement
statements.paraphrase: Courses prepare self-reflective, evidence-based and ethical practitioners; every course will offer an integrated curriculum of theory, research, skills training and personal and professional development, and must include an assessed and supervised placement.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure the course has an assessed, supervised placement as well as the integrated academic, skills and development strands.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: in-person and remote skills and core digital training
statements.paraphrase: Courses should equip students for in-person practice and can include remote practice; training should match the mode in which students will practise, and every course should include core training in electronic systems for data, literature, resources and communication.

forPractitioner.text: Match the training mode to how students will practise on placement and after, and include core digital training whatever the mode.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: inclusive teaching by a diverse team
statements.paraphrase: Inclusive practice by diverse trainers should run through all teaching and learning; activities should be designed authentically for the work, checked in advance for barriers to students with different needs, and staff should be open to tackling equality, diversity and inclusion with all stakeholders.

forPractitioner.text: Check every teaching activity for barriers in advance, and raise equality, diversity and inclusion with staff, students and placements alike.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: depth in a modality, its view of people and its heritage
statements.paraphrase: Courses usually give depth in one or more recognised modalities; this should include understanding that modality's account of human nature and its cultural roots as well as how to use it with clients, and an integrative course should be able to name its parts and show they fit together.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the chosen modality's view of human nature and its cultural history as well as its methods; if the course is integrative, set out its components and how they cohere.

forBeneficiary.text: You should understand how your chosen approach sees human nature and where it comes from culturally, as well as how to use it with clients.

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: respect for other approaches and modality-specific training
statements.paraphrase: Students need to develop awareness and respect for other therapeutic approaches and other mental health interventions, and course teams will adapt the style, emphasis and make-up of training to the modality and to the relevant professional body's requirements.

forPractitioner.text: Shape training to the needs of the modality and the professional body, while making sure students learn to respect other approaches.

forBeneficiary.text: You need to learn about and respect approaches to therapy and mental health other than your own.

statements.appliesTo: trainees on Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Research is a key skill for practitioners; at the least, graduates need enough awareness to use continuing development and to evaluate research in their field, and they should know quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods relevant to practice, usually through at least one small study.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the three families of research method, and give each student at least one small study, whether empirical, a systematic case study or a review.

forBeneficiary.text: You should know the main kinds of research method used in therapy, be able to judge research in your field, and usually carry out at least one small study yourself.

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Every course will provide for students' personal development, and should create chances to understand how the therapist's growth and emotional competence affect the relationship, which may include personal therapy or other suitable activities.

forPractitioner.text: Build personal development into every course, using groups, journals, residentials or personal therapy as suits the modality.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Training staff should help students find placements that fit their interests and stage, check placements and supervisors, require regular supervision during client work, consider how supervisors stay reflexive about privilege, power and oppression, and decide how placement feeds into assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Vet placements and supervisors, require regular supervision, and set out how placement evidence counts towards assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: qualified staff and suitable staff to student ratios
statements.paraphrase: Courses should be run by suitably qualified and experienced staff; because experiential work needs close containment, observation and care, staff to student ratios must suit students' learning needs, and the sector's experience supports ratios no higher than one to sixteen in experiential classes, with a clear rationale in all cases.

forPractitioner.text: Set and justify staff to student ratios for experiential work, keeping skills classes small enough for observation and feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.about: assessing theory and practice competence for the award
statements.paraphrase: Assessment will cover theory and skills against the course outcomes; in professional training practitioner competence will carry heavy weight and a satisfactory level will be a condition of the award, since the graduate is expected to be ready to practise at once.

forPractitioner.text: Weight practitioner competence heavily in assessment and make a satisfactory level a condition of the award.

forBeneficiary.text: Your assessment will cover both theory and skills, and you will need to reach a satisfactory level of practice competence to get your award.

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: inclusive, authentic assessment and its criteria
statements.paraphrase: Assessment may be formative or summative, in person or on secure platforms; it should be inclusive and true to the profession while keeping academic standards, and criteria should cover core skills and knowledge and broader professional skills such as risk awareness, teamwork, ethics and judgement.

forPractitioner.text: Write criteria that cover core counselling skills and wider professional skills, and make assessments inclusive and authentic.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.paraphrase: Quality assurance of assessment should be planned into design, moderation and review, with external examiners, critical friends, placements, employers and moderators, to share good practice.

forPractitioner.text: Involve external examiners, placements and employers in designing and reviewing assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses and their trainees
statements.paraphrase: Assessment should be used formatively to judge readiness for placement and summatively for the award; students must be assessed on skills, knowledge and personal resilience before they are approved to see real clients.

forPractitioner.text: Put a formal readiness check on skills, knowledge and resilience before any student sees clients.

forBeneficiary.text: Before you can work with real clients on placement, you must be assessed on your skills, knowledge and personal resilience.

statements.appliesTo: Counselling and Psychotherapy courses
statements.about: Annex D for achievement above the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do much better than the minimum; each institution decides what evidence shows this and should refer to Annex D, which describes the honours degree classes at FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10.

forPractitioner.text: Use Annex D alongside your own marking schemes to judge performance above the threshold.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: students on practice-facing honours courses
statements.about: competence in every part of the standard before completion
statements.paraphrase: The standards below are the threshold for honours at FHEQ level 6 or FQHEIS level 10, the least that students on professional courses must know, be and do to practise safely, ethically and effectively; successful students should be competent in every aspect before they complete.

forPractitioner.text: Assess every threshold standard before the award; competence in each is expected, not an average across them.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your course you should be competent in every part of the minimum standard for safe, ethical and effective practice, not just most of it.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: philosophical assumptions behind research and practice
statements.paraphrase: Grasp how underlying philosophical positions shape the different approaches to counselling research and practice, and weigh critically what this means for working in teams across disciplines.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the philosophical roots of the main approaches and research paradigms, and ask students to judge what those roots mean for multidisciplinary teamwork.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand how the beliefs underneath each approach shape research and practice, and you can judge what that means when you work with other professions.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Judge critically and put into practice the professional codes and organisational policies that govern practice, including those on diversity and equal opportunity.

forPractitioner.text: Have students test professional codes and agency policies against cases, including the parts on diversity and equal opportunity, and then apply them.

forBeneficiary.text: You can weigh up the codes and policies that govern your practice, including those on diversity and equality, and use them in real situations.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: government policy and guidance such as NICE
statements.paraphrase: Know how government policy and guidance, such as NICE guidelines, affect counselling services, research, mental health provision more widely and the well-being of clients.

forPractitioner.text: Include current policy and national clinical guidance in the curriculum, and ask students to trace their effects on services, research and clients.

forBeneficiary.text: You know how government policy and national guidance, such as NICE guidelines, shape therapy services, research and the care clients receive.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: power in relationships, groups and organisations
statements.paraphrase: See and understand how power shows itself in relationships, and reflect on how power dynamics work in groups, organisations and therapy and what they do to outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Use group work, placement and case material to help students name power dynamics and reflect on their effect on outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: You can spot how power works in relationships, groups, organisations and therapy, and think about how it changes what happens.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Be reflective about what counselling and psychotherapy do in present-day society, what they add and what pressures they face.

forPractitioner.text: Give students space to debate the profession's role, value and current challenges.

forBeneficiary.text: You think carefully about what therapy does for society today and the pressures it faces.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: examining one's own values and their effect on therapy
statements.paraphrase: Be thoughtful about, question and reflect on one's own values, beliefs, attitudes and behaviour, and on how they bear on therapeutic work.

forPractitioner.text: Use personal development groups and supervision for students to question their own values and trace their effect on client work.

forBeneficiary.text: You question and reflect on your own values, beliefs and habits, and on how they affect your work with clients.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Be able to see, and act on, professional responsibility to clients, employers, trainers, the professions and society.

forPractitioner.text: Help students map their duties to each party, and use placement to show them acting on those duties.

forBeneficiary.text: You can see where your professional responsibilities lie, to clients, employers, trainers, the profession and society, and you act on them.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: openness to diversity and to every client's rights
statements.paraphrase: Be open to diversity and welcome difference with regard to every client's rights and responsibilities, whatever their characteristics or identity, including but not only those the law protects.

forPractitioner.text: Make openness to difference something students show in practice and reflect on, going beyond the legally protected characteristics.

forBeneficiary.text: You are open to and welcome difference in every client, whatever their identity, not only in the ways the law protects.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: working within the social and political context
statements.paraphrase: See and work within the social, cultural and political setting of one's own practice and of the profession.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to locate their placement practice in its social, cultural and political context and show that they work with it.

forBeneficiary.text: You work with awareness of the social, cultural and political setting of your practice and of the profession.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: collaboration with supervisors and other professionals
statements.paraphrase: Form and keep professional relationships that suit the setting, and work with a supervisor and other professions to support and review client work, the wider practice and the growth of services.

forPractitioner.text: Assess how students collaborate with supervisors and other professionals on placement, including any contribution to how the service develops.

forBeneficiary.text: You build and keep working relationships with your supervisor and other professionals, and use them to support your client work and help the service improve.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Judge published counselling research critically and use a thorough, research-based body of knowledge consistently in practice.

forPractitioner.text: Require students to appraise studies and show, in case work, how research informs what they do with clients.

forBeneficiary.text: You can judge published research critically and let a sound, research-based understanding guide your work every time.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Work actively for equality, diversity and inclusion in practice and confront discrimination and prejudice at professional, organisational and systemic levels.

forPractitioner.text: Look for evidence that students act on equality and challenge prejudice, not only discuss it, on placement and in course life.

forBeneficiary.text: You actively promote equality and inclusion in your work and challenge discrimination and prejudice where you meet it, including in organisations.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: competencies for a self-directed professional life
statements.paraphrase: Build the academic, therapeutic and digital competencies for a fulfilling professional life that one directs oneself.

forPractitioner.text: Help students plan the academic, therapeutic and digital skills they will need to shape their own careers.

forBeneficiary.text: You build the academic, therapeutic and digital skills to shape a rewarding career of your own choosing.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Grow the capacity to adjust sensibly to changing settings and to uncertainty.

forPractitioner.text: Expose students to change, such as a move to remote work, and assess how they adapt.

forBeneficiary.text: You can adjust sensibly when your setting changes or when things are uncertain.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand and work with many-sided models of mental distress that respect different worldviews and frameworks and the client's own view, across biomedical, psychological, social, political and cultural accounts.

forPractitioner.text: Teach biomedical, psychological, social, political and cultural accounts of distress side by side, with the client's own account at the centre.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand several ways of explaining mental distress, from medical to social and cultural, and you keep the client's own view at the centre.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: the limits of one's chosen model
statements.paraphrase: See where one's chosen model may fall short with particular clients and try to reduce those shortfalls where possible.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to name cases where their core model struggles and say what they would do about it.

forBeneficiary.text: You can see where your chosen approach may not fit a particular client and look for ways to make up for that.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: other professional perspectives on mental health
statements.paraphrase: Acknowledge and respect a range of views on mental health, including those of other professions and agencies.

forPractitioner.text: Bring in other professions' views of mental health and ask students to engage with them respectfully.

forBeneficiary.text: You recognise and respect other views on mental health, including those of other professions and agencies.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: the social role of mental health services
statements.paraphrase: Understand and judge what mental health and counselling services do in society, and consider critically how social, political and economic forces affect present-day practice.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to analyse a service in its policy and economic setting and judge how those forces shape practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand what therapy services do in society and can think critically about how money, politics and social change shape them.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand and critically weigh how different theories treat the relationship, and what follows for skilled client work and for work with other professions.

forPractitioner.text: Compare how several approaches treat the relationship and link each to practice with clients and colleagues.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand and can compare how different approaches think about the relationship, and what that means for your work with clients and colleagues.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: openness to other approaches for good working relationships
statements.paraphrase: Be open to, and value, a range of approaches, so as to build and keep respectful working relationships with colleagues and good alliances with clients.

forPractitioner.text: Encourage students to learn from approaches other than their own and show that openness with peers and clients.

forBeneficiary.text: You are open to approaches other than your own, which helps you work well with colleagues and build alliances with clients.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: awareness of one's own and unconscious bias
statements.paraphrase: Be consciously aware of one's own biases and alert to unconscious bias linked to context, gender, age, ethnicity, origin, culture, class, ability, sexual orientation, religion and belief.

forPractitioner.text: Use reflective tasks and supervision for students to name their biases and watch for unconscious ones across the full range of identities.

forBeneficiary.text: You are aware of your own biases and alert to hidden ones about people's identity, background, ability, sexuality or faith.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: research-informed responses that respect client preference
statements.paraphrase: Use a range of responses, strategies and interventions grounded in research to shape practice that is sensitive to what clients need and prefer.

forPractitioner.text: Teach a repertoire of evidence-based interventions and assess whether students choose among them with the client's needs and wishes in mind.

forBeneficiary.text: You use a range of research-based responses and techniques, chosen with care for what each client needs and wants.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Use reflective practice, such as supervision, to notice and show awareness of one's own conscious bias and to check practice for signs of unconscious bias, so that therapy is anti-discriminatory.

forPractitioner.text: Make bias a standing item in supervision and reflective logs, and look for evidence that students act on what they find.

forBeneficiary.text: You use supervision and reflection to notice your own bias and check your work for hidden bias, so that your practice treats every client fairly.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Become aware of one's own enterprising capacities in therapeutic work, with the drive and discipline to use them flexibly as contexts change.

forPractitioner.text: Help students identify their own enterprising strengths in therapy settings and plan how to use them.

forBeneficiary.text: You know your own enterprising strengths in therapy work and have the drive to use them as situations change.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Understanding people and their experiences

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Show initiative, independence and responsibility.

forPractitioner.text: Assess initiative and independent judgement on placement and in projects.

forBeneficiary.text: You show initiative, work independently and take responsibility.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know one's personal and professional strengths and limits as they bear on practice.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to assess their own strengths and limits with evidence from practice and feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: You know your strengths and limits as a person and as a practitioner, and how they affect your work.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know what one needs to look after oneself and build suitable ways of supporting and caring for oneself.

forPractitioner.text: Have students write and review a self-care plan, and check it in supervision.

forBeneficiary.text: You know what you need to stay well and have workable ways to look after yourself.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know when referring a client to another service is the right step.

forPractitioner.text: Use case discussion to rehearse referral decisions and the routes available.

forBeneficiary.text: You can tell when it is right to refer a client to another service.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Be able to use supervision as a core part of practice that supports both the client work and the practitioner's growth.

forPractitioner.text: Make the use of supervision visible in assessment, not only the hours logged.

forBeneficiary.text: You use supervision as a central part of your practice, for your clients' sake and for your own growth.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Be able to supervise oneself, questioning one's values, beliefs, attitudes and behaviour and their effect on the work.

forPractitioner.text: Teach self-supervision methods and ask students to show them in process notes.

forBeneficiary.text: You can supervise yourself, questioning your own values and habits and how they affect your work with clients.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: commitment to ongoing development and fitness to practise
statements.paraphrase: Keep up a steady commitment to growing personally and professionally, self-awareness and fitness to practise included.

forPractitioner.text: Track personal and professional development through the course and treat fitness to practise as an ongoing matter.

forBeneficiary.text: You stay committed to your own development, personal and professional, including your self-awareness and fitness to practise.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: See when one needs personal support or therapy and take it up as fitting.

forPractitioner.text: Make routes to personal therapy and support clear, and help students judge when to use them.

forBeneficiary.text: You can tell when you need personal support or therapy and you take it up.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Use supervision to deepen understanding of practice and to strengthen and safeguard one's own well-being.

forPractitioner.text: Look for evidence that students use supervision to learn and to protect themselves, not only to report cases.

forBeneficiary.text: You use supervision to understand your practice better and to protect your own well-being.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: the ethical and legal contexts of practice
statements.paraphrase: Understand the main ethical and legal settings of practice, which means knowing the points that follow.

forPractitioner.text: Cover the ethical and legal ground in the points that follow explicitly and check it in assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand the main ethical and legal rules your practice works within.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: law relevant to practice, including online work
statements.paraphrase: Know the legal principles that bear on practice, such as data protection and child protection, including differences across the UK nations and international law when working online.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the law on data and child protection with its devolved variations and the international issues of online work.

forBeneficiary.text: You know the legal principles that affect your practice, such as data and child protection, including how they differ across the UK and abroad when you work online.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know the ethical frameworks, codes and good-practice guidance of professional associations, and the professional requirements, such as for supervision, that relevant bodies set.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the main professional codes and the requirements they set, such as for supervision, and compare them.

forBeneficiary.text: You know the ethical codes and guidance of the professional associations and what they require of you, for example in supervision.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know, where they apply, the policies and procedures of the agency one works in.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to learn and use their placement agency's policies.

forBeneficiary.text: You know the policies and procedures of the agency you work in.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: keeping up with changes in law and guidance
statements.paraphrase: Know about changes in the law and where to find current information, so that practice follows the latest ethical and legal guidance.

forPractitioner.text: Teach students where to find updates on law and ethics and how to keep their practice current.

forBeneficiary.text: You keep up with changes in law and guidance and know where to look so your practice stays current.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know what follows from having to break confidentiality, and be clear what must be disclosed and to whom.

forPractitioner.text: Rehearse confidentiality breaches through cases, with clear lines on what must be passed on and to whom.

forBeneficiary.text: You know what it means to have to break confidentiality, and you are clear what you must pass on and to whom.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand what follows from at least one ethical decision-making model suited to counselling and psychotherapy.

forPractitioner.text: Teach at least one decision-making model and have students apply it to dilemmas.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand at least one model for making ethical decisions in therapy and can use it.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Be committed to ethical work, matching practice to justice, integrity, trustworthiness, doing good, avoiding harm and self-care.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to show how core ethical principles guide their placement decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You are committed to working ethically, guided by justice, integrity, trust, doing good, avoiding harm and caring for yourself.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Practise under a named ethical code and act with care in line with its principles.

forPractitioner.text: Require students to name the code they work under and show its principles in their decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You work under a named ethical code and act thoughtfully in line with its principles.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Analyse, question and think through ethical dilemmas that arise in practice, with a supervisor or other suitable professionals as needed.

forPractitioner.text: Use real or simulated dilemmas and assess how students reason through them with supervisory input.

forBeneficiary.text: You can analyse and think through ethical dilemmas that come up in practice, drawing on your supervisor or others when needed.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: safety of client, therapist and setting
statements.paraphrase: Provide therapy with proper attention to the safety of client and therapist and to whether the setting is suitable.

forPractitioner.text: Check placement settings and students' risk practice for the safety of both client and therapist.

forBeneficiary.text: You provide therapy with care for your client's safety and your own, and for whether the setting is right.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Keep records with diligence, since records matter for the quality and safety of therapy.

forPractitioner.text: Assess the quality of students' notes as part of practice competence.

forBeneficiary.text: You keep careful records, knowing they matter for the quality and safety of therapy.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Handle records in line with the law, statutory requirements, professional information-governance standards and clients' legal rights.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the legal and governance rules for records, including clients' rights of access.

forBeneficiary.text: You handle records in line with the law, professional standards and your clients' legal rights.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Handle records properly across their life: accurate notes on paper or screen, secure storage, timely and purposeful sharing, and secure destruction.

forPractitioner.text: Cover the full record cycle, from writing to secure disposal, and check it on placement.

forBeneficiary.text: You handle records properly from start to finish: accurate notes, safe storage, careful sharing and secure disposal.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: demands of online and technology-mediated work
statements.paraphrase: Handle and meet suitably the practical, legal and ethical demands of online therapy and of all communication through technology.

forPractitioner.text: Include online practice in teaching on ethics and law, and assess students' handling of it.

forBeneficiary.text: You handle the practical, ethical and legal demands of working online and of any contact with clients through technology.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: contracting on confidentiality and data across settings
statements.paraphrase: Work within ethical and legal limits, contracting with clients on confidentiality and data protection in different working environments, including the points that follow.

forPractitioner.text: Teach contracting on confidentiality and data for in-person and remote work, and assess it in practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You agree with clients how confidentiality and data protection work in your setting, staying within ethical and legal limits.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Set out the limits of confidentiality, remote work included.

forPractitioner.text: Check that students state confidentiality limits clearly, including for remote work.

forBeneficiary.text: You make clear to clients where confidentiality ends, including when you work remotely.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: helping clients stay safe with data and platforms
statements.paraphrase: Be able to tell clients how to keep safe as to data, platforms, equipment and their physical surroundings.

forPractitioner.text: Give students a checklist for advising clients on safe remote set-ups.

forBeneficiary.text: You can tell clients how to stay safe with their data, devices, platform and surroundings.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know current digital platforms, digital accessibility and suitable technology for the profession, and the limits of their security for remote work.

forPractitioner.text: Review platforms with students for accessibility and security, and keep this current.

forBeneficiary.text: You know the main digital platforms and tools for therapy, how accessible they are, and where their security falls short.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Agree carefully on any recording of sessions by either party, and be able to explain what such recording means.

forPractitioner.text: Include recording in contracting role-plays.

forBeneficiary.text: You agree carefully with clients about any recording of sessions and can explain what it means.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Talk through data security and privacy for remote work, in light of the client's circumstances and any vulnerabilities.

forPractitioner.text: Teach students to tailor privacy discussions to each client's situation.

forBeneficiary.text: You talk through data security and privacy with clients you see remotely, taking account of their situation.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Keep the remote relationship intact when the technology breaks down.

forPractitioner.text: Agree with students a plan for dropped connections and rehearse it.

forBeneficiary.text: You keep the therapeutic relationship safe and steady when the technology breaks down.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Use intuitive judgement and find creative, new ways to deal with problems and ethical dilemmas, with integrity and compassion.

forPractitioner.text: Value creative problem-solving in case work, alongside rule-based ethics.

forBeneficiary.text: You use your judgement and find creative ways to handle problems and dilemmas, with integrity and compassion.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: safe boundaries in all professional relationships
statements.paraphrase: Understand what makes boundaries safe, responsive and therapeutic in every relationship: with clients, supervisors, tutors, colleagues and employers.

forPractitioner.text: Teach boundaries across all the relationships of training, not only those with clients.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand what safe, responsive boundaries look like with clients, supervisors, tutors, colleagues and employers.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Think about how to spot breaches of boundaries so that clear professional limits keep practice safe and effective.

forPractitioner.text: Use cases of breaches, small and large, for students to learn the warning signs.

forBeneficiary.text: You think about how to spot when a boundary is crossed, so you can keep clear limits and work safely.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Know contracting as part of an ethical, professional process and understand what a therapeutic contract is for and what it contains.

forPractitioner.text: Have students draft and critique a therapeutic contract.

forBeneficiary.text: You know why contracting matters ethically and what a therapeutic contract is for and should include.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: responsive boundaries that keep practice safe
statements.paraphrase: Recognise and understand how complex boundary work is, keeping boundaries responsive while making sure practice stays safe and ethical.

forPractitioner.text: Discuss cases where flexibility and firmness pull against each other.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand how complicated boundaries can be, and keep them responsive while staying safe and ethical.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand what employment law, policy and guidance mean for providing therapy in voluntary, community, statutory and private settings.

forPractitioner.text: Include employment law and policy in teaching on service settings.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand how employment law and policy affect therapy work in voluntary, community, public and private settings.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand the complexity and risk of sexual issues and dynamics in therapy and use this to keep boundaries safe and prevent sexual boundary violations.

forPractitioner.text: Teach sexual dynamics in therapy directly, with clear guidance on preventing violations.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand the risks when sexual issues or feelings arise in therapy and use that to keep boundaries safe.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: awareness of challenges in the work
statements.paraphrase: Be aware of the difficulties that may come up in therapeutic work.

forPractitioner.text: Prepare students for common difficulties before placement.

forBeneficiary.text: You are aware of the difficulties that can come up in therapy.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: confidence with change while holding boundaries
statements.paraphrase: Be confident in meeting changes and difficulties in the relationship therapeutically while keeping clear boundaries.

forPractitioner.text: Assess how students respond to shifts in the relationship without losing boundaries.

forBeneficiary.text: You respond with confidence when the relationship changes or gets difficult, while keeping clear boundaries.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Set and keep suitable professional boundaries throughout therapy and once it has ended.

forPractitioner.text: Include contact after ending in teaching on boundaries.

forBeneficiary.text: You set and keep proper boundaries throughout therapy and after it ends.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Work with the contract's limits and benefits and turn them to therapeutic use.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to show how they used the contract in the work, not only that they had one.

forBeneficiary.text: You use the limits and benefits of your contract with clients as part of the therapy.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Set and keep fitting personal and professional limits in online relationships with clients or patients, by making sure of the points that follow.

forPractitioner.text: Teach online boundaries, including social media, as part of professional conduct.

forBeneficiary.text: You set and keep proper boundaries with clients online, as the points that follow describe.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: separating personal and professional presence online
statements.paraphrase: Take reasonable care to keep one's personal and professional presence on social media apart where mixing them could create harmful dual relationships.

forPractitioner.text: Review students' social media practice as part of professional readiness.

forBeneficiary.text: You take care to keep your personal and professional social media apart, so that clients cannot be harmed by a dual relationship.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Make sure any public online communication fits one's own ethical framework or code.

forPractitioner.text: Check students' public posts and profiles against their code.

forBeneficiary.text: You make sure anything you post publicly online fits your ethical code.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: a secure frame for the work
statements.paraphrase: Create and keep a secure frame for therapy.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the elements of the frame and assess how students hold it.

forBeneficiary.text: You create and hold a secure frame for the work.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Agree a suitable contract with the client using all the information available.

forPractitioner.text: Assess contracting in recorded or observed practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You agree a suitable contract with each client, using everything you know about them.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Recognise and work with breaks and holidays and their effect on the relationship and process, arranging for clients to get support in an emergency.

forPractitioner.text: Teach planning for breaks, including emergency cover for clients.

forBeneficiary.text: You plan for breaks and holidays, notice how they affect the work, and make sure clients can get help in an emergency.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand why arrangements are needed for one's own sudden or unplanned absence or ending, have made them, and tell the client about them.

forBeneficiary.text: You have arrangements in place in case you suddenly cannot work, and you tell your clients about them.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Adjust suitably to different contracted time frames, both open-ended and time-limited.

forBeneficiary.text: You adjust your work to fit both open-ended and time-limited contracts.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Handle contact with outside agencies and professionals as the client's interest requires.

forBeneficiary.text: You handle contact with outside agencies and professionals in your client's interest.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): Boundaries and contracting

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Take an enquiring, critical and forward-looking approach to professional challenges, aware of social and therapeutic responsibility.

forBeneficiary.text: You meet professional challenges with curiosity, a critical eye and a view to the future, mindful of your responsibilities.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Understand the ideas and steps of client assessment, as the points that follow set out.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand what client assessment is and how it is done, as the points that follow set out.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Be able to define and explain client assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Ask students to define assessment in the terms of their own model.

forBeneficiary.text: You can define and explain what client assessment means.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: perspectives on assessment tools and outcome measures
statements.paraphrase: Understand the political, philosophical and theoretical views on assessment tools and outcome measures and judge, from research, what they mean for present-day practice.

forPractitioner.text: Debate outcome measures from several viewpoints, drawing on research.

forBeneficiary.text: You understand the arguments about assessment tools and outcome measures and can judge from research what they mean for practice.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: contexts of assessment, law and agency policy

forBeneficiary.text: You can discuss critically where and how assessment happens, with attention to ethics, law and agency rules.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: an assessment approach that fits one's model

forBeneficiary.text: You know at least one way of assessing that fits your approach and can explain how it shapes your work with a client.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: risk and protective factors for client safety

statements.paraphrase: Carry out a thorough evaluation of the client's needs and goals.

forBeneficiary.text: You evaluate thoroughly what each client needs and wants from therapy.

statements.paraphrase: Build a conceptualisation or formulation of what may be going on for the client, drawing on theory and on the work as it unfolds.

forBeneficiary.text: You build an understanding of what may be going on for a client, drawing on theory and on the work as it develops.

statements.paraphrase: Identify and weigh the risks the client presents with.

forBeneficiary.text: You identify and weigh any risks a client brings.

statements.appliesTo: graduates with honours in Counselling and Psychotherapy

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): The therapeutic relationship

forBeneficiary.text: You understand how power, oppression and privilege can affect the therapeutic relationship.

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): The therapeutic relationship

statements.about: respect for sexual diversity and difference

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): The therapeutic relationship

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): The therapeutic relationship

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): The therapeutic relationship

headingPath: Threshold level (3rd class): The therapeutic relationship

forBeneficiary.text: You recognise and work with what holds the alliance together, such as motivation, commitment and the contract.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: audit and evaluation to improve therapy
statements.paraphrase: Use audit and evaluation methods to help improve the process and outcomes of therapy.

forPractitioner.text: Include a service audit or evaluation task.

forBeneficiary.text: You use audit and evaluation to help improve how therapy is done and what it achieves.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Design, plan, carry out and evaluate a substantial empirical study or systematic review that answers a relevant question and adds to knowledge in the field.

forPractitioner.text: Supervise a substantial study through each stage, from question to evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: You design, carry out and evaluate a substantial research study that answers a real question and adds to what is known.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.about: reflexive use of self for in-depth work
statements.paraphrase: Use reflexivity, self-awareness and the self therapeutically to work in depth in the relationship and process.

forPractitioner.text: Assess depth of reflexive work in recorded sessions and supervision.

forBeneficiary.text: You use reflexivity, self-awareness and yourself to work in depth with clients.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in Counselling and Psychotherapy
statements.paraphrase: Facilitate or contain intense emotion in a highly charged encounter.

forPractitioner.text: Prepare students to hold strong emotion, with supervision close at hand.

forBeneficiary.text: You can stay with and contain strong emotion when a session becomes highly charged.
